instruction: Create a new 640x480 image in GIMP and export it as a PNG file named 'new_image.png' to the Desktop.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to convert RAW image to JPEG using GIMP. GIMP showed error 'no RAW loader installed'. Model dismissed error, installed darktable and dcraw via terminal, attempted CLI conversions, explored GIMP Filters menu, tried File > Open dialog. All attempts failed after 50 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate GIMP menus (File, Edit, Filters), open/close dialogs, use terminal commands, install packages via apt, browse file system in GIMP Open dialog, interact with GIMP UI elements
metadata.failure_analysis: Original task was intentionally infeasible - GIMP cannot open RAW files without external RAW loader plugins. Model spent all 50 turns trying workarounds that didn't succeed.
metadata.task_rationale: Decomposed the original 'convert and export' task into a simpler 'create new and export' task. Model demonstrated ability to navigate GIMP File menu and use dialogs. Creating a new image bypasses the RAW loading issue entirely.
metadata.explanation: Task asks model to create a new 640x480 image via File > New and export it as PNG to Desktop. Evaluator uses official check_image_size metric with vm_file getter to download the exported file and verify its dimensions are exactly 640x480.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter (vm_file) correctly targets /home/user/Desktop/new_image.png, matching the instruction's required file name and location.
Metric (check_image_size) correctly receives the rules dict {'width': 640, 'height': 480} and accesses rule.get('width') and rule.get('height') directly - proper parameter handling for type='rule'.
Dimension verification (640x480) exactly matches the instruction requirements.
File existence is implicitly verified: if the file doesn't exist, vm_file getter returns None and check_image_size returns 0.0.
PNG format is implicitly verified by the file extension and successful PIL Image.open().

Minor note: evaluator does not explicitly verify the file is in PNG format (could theoretically be another format saved with .png extension), but this is extremely unlikely given GIMP's export behavior.
